catalog_quote: [Kato 2003 p.633-634] The syllable structure of the Hpa-an dialect can be represented as C1(C2)V1(V2)(C3)/T, where C1 is an onset consonant, C2 is the second member of a cluster, V is a vowel, C3 is a coda, and T is a tone. ... There are four tones: High-level ... Pronounced with normal voice. Mid-level ... Pronounced with breathy voice. It is sometimes accompanied by arising contour especially in utterance final position. Low-level ... Pronounced with normal voice. Falling ... Pronounced with slightly creaky voice. ... The Hpa-an dialect has atonic syllables, in which /ə/ is the only permitted vowel, and which never occur in utterance final position. [Kato 2004 sec. 2.5-2.6] ポー・カレン語の声調素には次に掲げる四つがある。... 高平調 ... 中平調 ... 低平調 ... 下降調 ... ポー・カレン語には声調を持たない音節がある。これを軽声音節 (atonic syllable) と呼ぶ。表記上は、声調符号を付さないことによってこれを示す。軽声音節に現れる母音は、/ə/ のみである。軽声音節が発話末に現れることは決してない。... audit.reasoning: The classification (tonal; no word-stress rule; domain unstated) rests on the 603-page reference grammar of exactly this dialect by its principal describer (Kato 2004), held held by the project, with the deciding Japanese passage confirmed verbatim at pp. 21-23 (secs 2.5-2.6) and the English cross-check (Kato 2003) confirmed in the djvu text we hold. I downloaded and read the remaining Kato phonology sources (1995 LTBA via scanned, 2019 Mouton preprint, 2021 Karenic typology preprint): all state four lexical tones on full syllables plus toneless /ə/-only atonic syllables that cannot be utterance-final, and none posits a word-stress or accent rule; Kato 2021 merely glosses atonal syllables as 'phonetically unstressed and short' and sesquisyllables as unstressed+stressed, which is the full-vs-minor asymmetry the record already describes. sources.citation: Kato, Atsuhiko. 1995. The phonological systems of three Pwo Karen dialects. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 18(1): 63-103.
sources.quote: 'There are four tonemes in the Hpa-an dialect: high-level [55], mid-level [33], low-level [11], falling [51] ... accompanied by laryngealization'; 'The Hpa-an dialect has atonic syllables, in which /ə/ is the only permitted vowel, and which never occur in utterance final position.' Only use of 'stress': numeral 'one' 'appears in the unstressed form /lə-/' before a classifier (p. 80). No stress/accent section.
sources.note: Glottolog's ranked phonology reference for pwoe1235 (Hpa-an sec. 2); was not yet obtained; now downloaded and read, confirms four tonemes + atonic /ə/ syllables, no stress section.

sources.citation: Kato, Atsuhiko. 2021. Typological profile of Karenic languages. In P. Sidwell & M. Jenny (eds.), The Languages and Linguistics of Mainland Southeast Asia, 337-367. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton (author preprint, ch. 18).
sources.quote: 'EPK (the Hpa-an dialect) has four tones'; 'EPK has atonal syllables, which are phonetically unstressed and short, and cannot occur utterance-finally ... The only vowel that can occur in an atonal syllable is /ə/ ... EPK has many disyllabic words that have an atonal first syllable. These are sesquisyllabic in Matisoff's (1973) terms, in that they are composed of the unstressed first syllable and the stressed second syllable.' Also: first syllables of some disyllables may reduce to atonal in rapid speech (/khʊ́lòɴ ~ khəlòɴ/ 'mountain').
sources.locator: sec. 18.2, preprint the text (EPK four tones) and 346-356 (atonal syllables)
sources.note: Most recent statement by the dialect authority; the only Kato text that uses the word 'stress' for Hpa-an (atonal syllables 'phonetically unstressed and short'; sesquisyllables = unstressed + stressed syllable) -- useful wording for the record's tone_note/caution, does not change the tonal coding.

sources.citation: Kato, Atsuhiko. 2019. Pwo Karen. In A. Vittrant & J. Watkins (eds.), The Mainland Southeast Asia Linguistic Area, 131-175. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter (author preprint).
sources.quote: 'The Hpa-an dialect has four tones: High-level [ma55], Mid-level [ma̤33~334], Low-level [ma11], Falling [ma51]'; syllable C1(C2)V1(V2)(ɴ)/(T), 'T is bracketed because Pwo Karen has atonic syllables, which always end with the vowel /ə/ ... Atonic syllables cannot appear in an utterance-final position'; 'Pwo Karen also has a lot of sesquisyllabic words, that is, disyllabic words with an atonal first syllable'. No word-stress rule.
sources.locator: sec. 2.1 'Suprasegmental phonology' p. 133; sec. 2.2 p. 134; sec. 3.1 p. 136
sources.note: Latest English sketch of the Hpa-an dialect with IPA tone values; downloaded (author preprint) and read, confirms coding.

sources.citation: Phillips, Audra. 2000. West-Central Thailand Pwo Karen phonology. Papers from the 33rd International Conference on Sino-Tibetan Languages and Linguistics, Bangkok: Ramkhamhaeng University, 99-110.
sources.quote: For West-Central Thailand Pwo (Kanchanaburi; a different dialect under the same Glottolog languoid): 'Pwo Karen, for the most part, exhibits two rhythmic patterns in words. The first is the unstressed-stressed iambic pattern ... The other rhythmic pattern is combinations of major syllables where the first major syllable is stressed ... as in /mɨ mí/ sun'; atonic/proclitic [ə] morphemes are 'destressed variants ... due to the rhythmic patterns at the phrase and clause level'; 'As yet, evidence is limited on Pwo Karen rhythm'. Four phonemic tones (sec. 4.4.1). This is the account Kato 2004 sec.
sources.locator: sec. 3 'Stress and rhythm', p. 100 (page scan checked)
sources.note: The work Kato 2004 sec. 2.6 argues against; gives an explicit (impressionistic) word-rhythm statement for the Thailand Pwo variety grouped under the same glottocode (iambic minor+major; first-syllable stress in major+major words). Relevant if the catalog ever splits or annotates dialects; downloaded and read now.

sources.citation: Naruemon Chuensukon (1995). A phonological study of Pwo Karen at Huay-Hom-Nok Village, Tambon Th. Mahidol University.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The thesis describes the Pwo Karen of Huay-Hom-Nok Village, Lamphun Province, northern Thailand, i.e. a Northern Pwo Karen (Phlong) variety, not the Hpa-an dialect of Eastern Pwo Karen (Myanmar) that the catalog item pwoe1235 is named for. Glottolog attaches it to pwoe1235, which is why it was listed. For that Lamphun variety the statement is a clean fixed: final syllable rule (predictable, on the word-final major syllable, with secondary stress on minor syllables and zero on presyllables).
